key_insight: Entanglement-based positronium imaging is statistically demanding: double-Compton events retain only 0.1–0.6% of the quantum information limit for measuring polarisation correlation.
engineering_relevance: CZT detector design, multi-site sequence reconstruction and event-wise maximum likelihood can improve information recovery, but tissue discrimination remains limited by event counts.
method: Derive classical Fisher information for polarisation correlation κ and compare with the quantum limit.
Relate κ to positronium annihilation channels and tissue pick-off fractions.
Simulate pixelated CZT rings and compare event-wise maximum likelihood with the conventional ratio estimator.
evidence_signal: The model was checked against three published measurements and an independent GATE/Geant4 simulation; simulated double-Compton events carried 0.015 Fisher-information units on average.
watch_item: Under the studied ¹⁸F eight-module-ring conditions, distinguishing tissues by κ alone requires 6–74 times more decays than available, despite achievable ±0.01 precision in a 10-mm tumour.
paper_title: How many events does entanglement-based positronium imaging need? Information limits of Compton polarimetry with CZT detectors
